title: FREE SPEECH IS NOT A CRIME
music: Taut minimalist documentary underscore. Ticking muted pizzicato strings over a low sustained drone, 85 bpm, suspenseful but understated, no vocals, no drums, steady bed under narration.

segments.narration: Neptune Beach, twenty twenty-two. Stefen Wynn tells the police chief a city councilor and her husband committed a felony. They had not. A judge's order now lays it out.

overlays.text: Told the chief the councilor and her husband “had committed a felony.” The husband wasn’t in the room, and it wouldn’t have been a felony anyway.

sfx.prompt: old desk telephone receiver picked up, brief dial tone

segments.narration: Paonia, twenty twenty-six. March. He takes a resident's Facebook post to the police.

sfx.prompt: heavy rubber stamp pressed onto paper, single hit

segments.narration: April. Two voicemails. One asks him to fix the potholes on Third Street. Police: free speech. Unfounded.

overlays.text: “maybe you should fix the potholes on Third Street first. Have a great day.”

sfx.prompt: heavy rubber stamp pressed onto paper, single hit

segments.narration: May. A criminal complaint over a post reading eighty-six Wynn. Out of ten commenters, he names one: his critic's partner, who wrote, we have a lovely town. Police: not a victim, not a witness. Unfounded.

overlays.text: “We have a lovely town, so let’s have lovely people working to protect it.”
Wynn is “not a victim or a witness to a crime.”

sfx.prompt: heavy rubber stamp pressed onto paper, single hit

segments.narration: Four times, in two towns, he took his critics to the police. Four times, no crime.

sfx.prompt: soft deep cinematic boom hit, short

end.source: Sources: Wynn v. City of Neptune Beach, Order Granting Summary Judgment (Oct. 1, 2026); Paonia PD records P26-0191, P26-0289, P26-0323 (CCJRA, June 4, 2026)
